samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both guides are built from the samples. B gives each habit a limit ('one sentence, then move on', 'drop the jokes entirely' with upset customers) and has a say/don't-say pair for each, so a freelancer is less likely to overdo it. A is tighter, but its rewrite invents a day ('Tuesday') and a place ('front bench') even though it flags them. Both rewrites drop 'this weekend' and add care claims. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both guides draw on the samples and quote them, but A sets clearer limits on each habit: one sentence for an admission and only when it's true, at most one joke per piece, no jokes in complaints, and 'don't go so blunt that it's cold'. Both rewrites leave out 'this weekend' and add care claims, but B also invents a delivery day ('Tuesday') and a display spot ('front bench'). B flags those as placeholders, but they are still new facts in the rewrite. A's rewrite stays closer to the original facts and avoids the filler without translating it.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both guides quote the samples rather than relying on generic adjectives. In the rewrites, A keeps the core facts but adds a care claim (flagged, and it states the days only as 'every other day' after 'Closed Mondays'); B invents more (the Tuesday arrival, front bench, every-two-weeks watering) and drops 'this weekend'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both guides are built from quoted sample habits, but B ties nearly every habit to a clear limit (no spec sheets, no gloom, no piled-on tips, leave the aside out if it isn't natural, no jokes on money or hours). A gives limits for only a few habits. In the rewrite, A drops 'this weekend' and invents an arrival day, a bench location and a watering schedule. B keeps the weekend and the hours and uses a placeholder for the day, though it also adds care advice and rephrases Tuesday through Sunday as 'every other day'. Both answers flag what they invented.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both guides quote the samples well, but only B gives every habit an explicit limit (one admission, at most one aside, no aside when the news is bad, blunt about the plant and not the person). Both rewrites drop 'this weekend' and add care advice and 'Closed Mondays', which the original didn't contain, though each flags the care line.
